prompt: What does the opening of this gospel establish about who Jesus is?
options: He is a wise teacher raised up from among John the Baptist's own circle of disciples
He is the eternal Word of God who existed from the beginning and became flesh
He is an angel sent to announce the coming kingdom to the shepherds
He is a reincarnation of John the Baptist returned in a new body

prompt: What do Jesus' conversations with Nicodemus and the Samaritan woman have in common?
options: Both show Jesus offering spiritual transformation across social and religious boundaries
Both end with the listener publicly rejecting Jesus and reporting him to the authorities
Both take place inside the Jerusalem temple during a festival crowd
Both are private conversations that Jesus later denies ever having taken place

prompt: What pattern do Jesus' signs and teaching provoke among the religious leaders in this stretch of the gospel?
options: Immediate and unanimous belief among every Pharisee who witnesses a sign
Growing hostility and a determination to stop him
A formal invitation for him to teach permanently inside the Jerusalem temple
No reaction at all, since the leaders never hear about the signs

prompt: How does Jesus describe his relationship to his followers using imagery of light and shepherding?
options: As a distant ruler who never personally interacts with any of the people he governs from his throne
As one who guides and cares for those who belong to him, even at the cost of his own life
As a hired hand who abandons the sheep the moment danger comes near
As a judge who condemns wrongdoers publicly without offering any mercy

prompt: What effect does the raising of Lazarus have on the religious leaders' plans for Jesus?
options: It convinces the council to abandon their opposition to Jesus altogether
It has no effect at all, since word of it never reaches Jerusalem
It hardens their resolve, and Caiaphas prophesies Jesus must die for the nation
It causes them to arrest Lazarus instead of pursuing Jesus

prompt: What is the main purpose of Jesus' extended teaching to his disciples at the last supper?
options: To comfort and prepare them for his departure and the coming of the Holy Spirit
To announce a new set of dietary laws for the disciples to follow
To rebuke the disciples harshly for their repeated lack of faith
To explain the legal and political details of the coming Roman trial

prompt: How does John's account of Jesus' arrest and trial move from the garden to the cross?
options: Jesus is arrested, questioned by Jewish and Roman authorities, and crucified while Peter denies him
Jesus escapes the arresting soldiers and hides in Bethany until the crowds disperse
Jesus is tried only by Pilate, since no Jewish authorities are involved at all
Jesus is stoned to death by the temple crowd before Pilate can intervene

prompt: What is the climax of the resurrection accounts in the final two chapters?
options: Jesus never appears to anyone again once the empty tomb is discovered
The disciples conclude that Jesus' body was stolen and quietly stop following him
Jesus appears alive multiple times, overcomes Thomas's doubt, and restores Peter to service
Mary Magdalene is arrested by the temple guard for spreading a false report

prompt: What role does John the Baptist play in this gospel's opening chapters?
options: A rival prophet who actively competes with Jesus for his own following
A witness who points others to Jesus as the Lamb of God and the greater one to come
A Roman soldier personally assigned to guard Jesus during his ministry
A member of the Sanhedrin who formally condemns Jesus as a blasphemer

prompt: How does Nicodemus's relationship with Jesus change across the gospel?
options: He starts as an open, public follower of Jesus and ends up denying him under pressure
He begins as a cautious night visitor and later helps bury Jesus' body
He never appears again in the story after his conversation in chapter 3
He becomes one of the twelve apostles chosen to travel with Jesus

prompt: What ultimately happens to Peter after he denies Jesus three times?
options: He is expelled from the group of disciples and never mentioned again
Jesus never speaks to him again for the rest of the gospel
The risen Jesus restores him and commissions him to feed his sheep
He replaces Judas as treasurer of the group with no further consequence

prompt: What motivates Judas Iscariot's actions in the days leading up to Jesus' arrest?
options: He objects to Mary's costly gift and later leads soldiers to betray Jesus
He tries to quietly protect Jesus from the plotting religious authorities
He is a Roman citizen with no real connection to the Jewish leadership
He publicly confesses Jesus as the Christ shortly before betraying him

prompt: What does Caiaphas argue when the council debates what to do about Jesus after Lazarus is raised?
options: That Jesus should be crowned king immediately to calm the crowds
That it is better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish
That Jesus should be exiled from Judea rather than killed
That the council has no legal authority to act against Jesus at all

prompt: How does Pilate respond when he examines Jesus during the trial?
options: He immediately condemns Jesus to death without ever questioning him
He finds no guilt in Jesus but still hands him over to be crucified
He refuses outright to interrogate Jesus in any way
He releases Jesus unharmed and punishes the accusing crowd instead

prompt: What happens when the crowd is offered a choice between Jesus and Barabbas?
options: They ask Pilate to release both prisoners together as a gesture of peace
They demand that Barabbas, a robber, be released instead of Jesus
They demand that Jesus be released and Barabbas be crucified in his place
They refuse to choose at all and leave the decision entirely to Pilate

prompt: What role does Thomas play after the resurrection?
options: He immediately believes the other disciples' report without any hesitation
He doubts the resurrection until he sees and touches Jesus' wounds, then confesses him as Lord and God
He is the very first person to discover the empty tomb that morning
He denies to the other disciples that he ever doubted Jesus

prompt: What is Mary Magdalene's role in the resurrection narrative?
options: She is the first person the risen Jesus appears to, and she reports the news to the disciples
She helps Joseph of Arimathea prepare Jesus' body and seal the tomb
She is one of the twelve disciples chosen at the very start of the gospel
She is questioned and dismissed by the guards stationed at the tomb

prompt: What does Joseph of Arimathea do after Jesus' death?
options: He publicly denies knowing Jesus in order to protect his seat on the council
He asks Pilate for Jesus' body and provides a new tomb for burial
He leads the very soldiers who arrest Jesus in the garden
He is crucified alongside Jesus on a third cross

prompt: What common thread connects the seven miraculous signs Jesus performs in this gospel?
options: Each one is performed in secret, deliberately hidden from the surrounding crowds
Each one reveals Jesus' identity and points people toward believing in him
Each one is immediately followed by an attempt to arrest and execute him
Each one takes place outside the region of Galilee and Judea entirely

prompt: What do the seven 'I am' statements Jesus makes have in common?
options: Each one uses ordinary imagery to describe what Jesus provides for those who trust him
Each one is spoken only to the twelve disciples behind closed doors
Each one is immediately and universally rejected by everyone who hears it
Each one describes a distant future event rather than who Jesus is now

prompt: How does this gospel use the image of light and darkness?
options: Light represents Roman authority and darkness represents the nation of Israel
Light represents truth and life found in Jesus, while darkness represents rejecting him
Light and darkness are used only as literal descriptions of the time of day
Light represents the Jerusalem temple and darkness represents the local synagogue

prompt: What does 'born again' mean in Jesus' conversation with Nicodemus?
options: A literal second physical birth from one's own mother's womb
A spiritual rebirth by the Spirit that allows a person to see the kingdom of God
A yearly ceremonial washing performed by every worshiper at the temple
Formally becoming a registered member of the Pharisees

prompt: What does the image of the vine and branches teach about the relationship between Jesus and his disciples?
options: Disciples can bear lasting fruit only by remaining connected to Jesus
Branches that are cut off from the vine continue to bear fruit on their own
The vinedresser only tends and prunes the vine once every year
Fruit has no real connection to a disciple's closeness to Jesus

prompt: What does Jesus promise his disciples about the Holy Spirit in his farewell teaching?
options: That the Spirit will fully replace Jesus, so the disciples will no longer need him at all
That the Spirit will come as a helper to guide them into truth after Jesus departs
That the Spirit will only come to the disciples after they themselves have died
That the Spirit will appear visibly just once and then depart forever

prompt: What is the significance of Jesus' resurrection appearances at the end of the gospel?
options: They prove Jesus is alive and confirm the disciples' mission to continue his work
They are private visions experienced only by Mary Magdalene alone
They take place exclusively in Jerusalem and never anywhere in Galilee
They are described in the text as dreams rather than physical appearances
